VII. LOCAL SHORT TEPM USES AND LONG TEPM PRODUCTIVITY
The proposed alternate corridors as presented at the public hearings traversed areas along their routes that were largely agricultural in nature and undeveloped. However, if present trends continue it can be assumed that all of the undeveloped lands and agricultural lands near the airport will be changed to residential and commercial development. These private uses have already altered much of the landscape with the removal of trees, vegetation and the filling of lands to make them suitable for development.
Because this development in the vicinity of General Mitchell Field still continues, the early conversion of land from private use to public use as a transportation corridor would ensure improved and needed ground access to the airport.
The proposed facility will be in conformance with SEWPPC's regional land use and transportation plans and will serve to implement the Milwaukee County Jurisdictional Highway System Plan, and Milwaukee Area Transit Plan. These plans are actively being used for the development of all transportation systems in Milwaukee County and the City of Milwaukee. These plans have considered General Mitchell Field as a major air transportation facility and important land use concentration. General Mitchell Field will remain as the region's scheduled air carrier airport with future airport expansion limited to presently owned county land.
The Airport Spur fr eway was recommended to provide improved surface transportation to the region's only scheduled air transport airport and serve the passenger, employment and air cargo demands.
